humanities_role_explanation: The study targets iconographic classification of Christian saints using Iconclass, a core art-historical competence (identifying subject matter via attributes), rather than using artworks as generic image data. It is framed around Panofskyan iconography and metadata curation for digital humanities.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Images of paintings depicting Christian saints are paired with text prompts containing class labels or Iconclass descriptions. The model outputs a class label. The CSV metadata lists text only, but the paper's inputs are images plus text prompts.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Single-label classification of Christian saints in paintings (10 classes per dataset) under Test 1 (zero-shot with labels), Test 2 (zero-shot with Iconclass descriptions) and Test 3 (few-shot with five exemplars). This is recognition of saints via attributes rather than deeper iconological interpretation.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to a single task: single-label classification of Christian saints in paintings.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash, plus CLIP and SigLIP variants.

summary: The paper benchmarks CLIP, SigLIP, GPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 models on single-label classification of Christian saints across ArtDL, an ICONCLASS subset and a Wikidata subset, in zero-shot and few-shot settings. Multimodal LLMs beat fine-tuned ResNet50 baselines on ArtDL and ICONCLASS, but SigLIP does best on Wikidata. Class descriptions generally help, while few-shot exemplars mostly do not.
key_findings: Gemini-2.5 Pro peaked at 90.45% on ArtDL, outperforming the ResNet50 baseline (84.44%). On ICONCLASS it reached 84.82%, against a baseline of 40.46%. On Wikidata SigLIP-so400m was best at 66.29%, against a baseline of 43.97%. Descriptions generally improved zero-shot results, except for LLMs on Wikidata. Few-shot learning mostly lowered accuracy. Cross-dataset consistency was lower for LLMs (25-33%) than for contrastive models.
facets_explanation: Labels come from Iconclass codes already attached to the images in ArtDL, the ICONCLASS AI Test Set and Wikidata. Multi-saint and multi-label images were removed to keep a single label. Identifying the saint requires iconographic knowledge not given in the image. The paper does not discuss annotator disagreement.
results_explanation: The best score is Gemini-2.5 Pro on ArtDL Test 1 (90.45%), taken from Table 2. The largest input gap is the SigLIP-large Wikidata drop from 60.03% (labels) to 43.95% (descriptions), about 16 points. The larger gap comes from CLIP-ViT-L/14 on ArtDL, 30.58% to 44.31%, about 14 points, and from SigLIP-base on ArtDL, 48.71% to 68.19%, about 19.5 points. Across datasets the maximum observed is about 20 points, rounded here. Dataset and evaluation sizes sum 1,864 + 863 + 718 test images, although the baselines were evaluated on a 20% split. No human baseline is reported.
